rules.statement: A person occupying premises under a licence pending sale is not entitled to claim protection under the Rent Restriction Act if the sale does not occur.
rules.supporting_quote: "When a prospective purchaser of certain premises is permitted, pending the purchase to occupy the premises on payment of a stipulated sum of money his occupation is at best, that of a licencee and not that of a contractual tenant entitled to claim the protection of the Rent Restriction Act. If the contemplated sale does not take place, the duration of the licencee expires and the licencee becomes a trespasser liable to be ejected". As stated earlier on an examination of the evidence led in the instant case it appears to me that this is a case where the defendant-appellant has gone back on his oral agreement to sell the 320 property in suit. There is no evidence that he intended or in fact perpetrated a fraud. There is no evidence that the defendant-appellant enriched himself at the expense of the plaintiffs-respondents. In the circumstances, I am inclined to take the view that section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance would also apply to the instant case. In Don v Don (4) it was observed by Drieberg, J. rules.statement: Oral evidence of an informal promise to execute a written agreement is inadmissible under the statute of frauds where the refusal to sign is merely a refusal to honor such an informal promise.
